method: API evaluator 1.0: three caption-blind observers each received only the image inside the request; a coder, run 2 times, received only the contract and their answers split into numbered units and cited a unit for each finding; code verified every citation and computed the verdict, which passes only when every coding passes (scripts/lib/adjudication.mjs). AI review is not clinical approval.

observers.label: Caption-blind observer 1 (Claude)

answers.1: A drawing of a person's head and upper neck, seen from behind and slightly to the side (back-right view). The face is turned away so only the nose, eyebrow and cheek edge show at the right. Shoulders are cut off at the bottom.
answers.2: The hair on top and at the front is thick and brown; the side and back of the head are shaved very short, shown as fine stubble-like dashes. The skin looks smooth and intact, with no cut, scar, redness or bandage drawn. Two grey devices are worn: a round, flat disc sits on the shaved scalp above and behind the ear, roughly at the hairline where the long hair begins; a short coiled cord runs from it down and forward to a curved, bean-shaped unit that hooks over the top of the outer ear and rests in the crease behind the ear. The behind-the-ear unit has small buttons on its side and a tiny red dot near its top. The ear itself is uncovered and looks normal.
answers.3: No text, numbers, arrows, labels or symbols anywhere. The only small detail is the tiny red dot on the behind-the-ear device, which looks like an indicator light.
answers.4: A worried patient might read the disc on the scalp as something stuck into or through the skin after brain surgery, or as monitoring electrodes taped to the head, rather than a removable worn device.
